headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: Plane can ingest prompt content from awesome-prompts, but the pair lacks direct shared-write channels or documented automation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt-writing/content source, and Plane accepts file uploads plus hyperlinks/notes, so a user can bridge prompt text into Plane content that may be treated as instructions. There is no documented shared filesystem or direct parser bridge, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced. Plane’s broad egress increases exposure if injected content triggers outbound actions.
conditions: IF a user copies prompt text from awesome-prompts into Plane notes, tasks, or uploaded files
IF Plane content is later interpreted as instructions by an operator or downstream workflow
mitigations: Restrict pasted prompt content to a quarantined notes area
Add a manual review step before any Plane task is actioned
Label imported prompt libraries as untrusted
Disable automatic processing of uploaded text files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts touches no data classes and has no network egress, while Plane touches issues, tasks, files, notes, and has broad egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is limited to operator-mediated transfer rather than default exfiltration. The main risk is accidental inclusion of sensitive Plane content in copied prompts or uploads.
conditions: IF sensitive Plane issues, files, or notes are manually copied into awesome-prompts workflows
IF Plane uploads are exported into prompt repositories or chat contexts
mitigations: Avoid copying Plane artifacts into prompt libraries
Redact issue text before reuse
Limit uploads to non-sensitive files
Use separate accounts/workspaces for the two tools
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exported task text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, while Plane has write_filesystem false and only supports multiple instances plus API/file surfaces. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write path documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF an external integration adds shared state not present in the profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant shared write credentials
Review any orchestrator for locking semantics
requires-engineering: add resource-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can consume files, notes, and hyperlinks, so it could treat output derived from awesome-prompts as authoritative if an operator feeds it forward. awesome-prompts is a prompt repository rather than a verifier, so its content may be reused without validation. The pair lacks documented automation, so the cascade is inferred, but the blast radius can span multiple work items.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-prompts are pasted into Plane tasks or notes
IF Plane workflows act on those tasks without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from prompt content
Mark imported content as advisory only
Separate drafting from execution queues
Add checklist validation for task creation
requires-engineering: add source-confidence metadata

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-prompts has no touched data classes, and Plane’s profile does not specify regulated data handling or a conflicting jurisdiction, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into Plane without a matching policy
IF deployment jurisdiction or retention settings differ from the documented profiles
mitigations: Classify data before use
Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review retention settings
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA terms
